# macdoc

> A safe, local-first macOS CLI that explains why a developer Mac is full and slow, and gets space back without surprises.

macdoc scans your Mac, shows where space and memory go, and suggests cleanups from a fixed recipe catalog. It deletes nothing by itself: a person approves each removal at a real terminal.

## Commands

Read-only (safe to run any time):
- `macdoc` (overview when piped), `macdoc scan`, `macdoc reclaim [toolchain] [--toolchains] [--categories]` (read-only without a terminal; at a real terminal it asks which risk types to clean (tick the boxes, then Enter on the Clean button; a typed answer of Enter alone is SAFE only; each RISKY item needs its ID typed), which agents must never answer; it never offers an installed app, that is `retire`), `macdoc retire`, `macdoc explore [path] [--growth] [--projects]`, `macdoc vitals [--memory]`, `macdoc log`
- Every command supports `--json` (schemas in `schema/`).

Removal (Terminal, person only):
- There is no `macdoc apply`, `refresh` or plan command (ADR 0015). `macdoc reclaim` and the dashboard are how things get cleaned; `macdoc reclaim --tier safe|caution --yes` and the dashboard's `/reclaim` clean quarantine moves with no prompt, and agents must never run them.
- `macdoc quarantine restore|purge` also belong to the person.

## MCP server

`macdoc mcp` lets an AI assistant diagnose and suggest what to clean. It has no plan or apply tool and cannot delete, move, restore, accept a path or run a command. The person cleans with `macdoc reclaim` in Terminal.
